body:
<!-- generated-release-notes v1 -->

Claude thinking tokens were being billed at roughly 1.7 times the actual Anthropic cost. That is fixed in this release, and cache writes are now priced correctly too. If your workspace uses AI features, credit usage will drop from this version forward.

Installed app and marketplace pages show their content again. You can see what data objects, automations, and interface pieces an app includes before or after installing it. SAML providers saved with PEM certificates now authenticate correctly.

The Security and Privacy settings pages have been reorganized. Iframe origins and media access use table-style inputs with favicons, the AI card links to the agents and model tiers it affects, and the compliance section opens with a cleaner layout.

## 🌟 Highlights

- Claude thinking tokens were billed at about 1.7× the Anthropic rate — that is now corrected, and cache writes are priced correctly too. ([#29976](https://github.com/twentyhq/twenty/pull/29976))
- Installed app and marketplace pages show the full content an app adds — data, automations, interface pieces — after being missing since earlier this year. ([#29707](https://github.com/twentyhq/twenty/pull/29707))
- SAML providers saved with a PEM certificate now authenticate correctly. ([#29993](https://github.com/twentyhq/twenty/pull/29993))
- The workspace assistant's configured name and avatar now appear in inbox message headers, mentions, and previews. ([#29841](https://github.com/twentyhq/twenty/pull/29841))
- The AI data policy controls in Privacy settings no longer flash or remount when you save an unrelated setting. ([#29989](https://github.com/twentyhq/twenty/pull/29989))
- The "Follow up on closing deals" Getting Started step no longer appears for members who lack the Workflows permission. ([#29992](https://github.com/twentyhq/twenty/pull/29992))

## ✨ New features

- Installed app and marketplace pages show the full list of resources an app adds — grouped as Data, Interface, Automation and AI, Access, and Packaging — after the content tabs were removed earlier this year. ([#29707](https://github.com/twentyhq/twenty/pull/29707)) by @ijreilly
- Getting Started is now enabled by default for all newly activated workspaces. ([#29964](https://github.com/twentyhq/twenty/pull/29964)) by @etiennejouan
- The book-a-call step for new teams moves from the onboarding flow into Getting Started, so it no longer interrupts the flow just before the plan step. ([#29980](https://github.com/twentyhq/twenty/pull/29980)) by @etiennejouan

## 💅 Improvements & UX

- AI-generated component previews are now type-checked before they run, so wrong props, missing fields, or bad SDK calls surface as source-level errors in chat instead of silent runtime failures. ([#29412](https://github.com/twentyhq/twenty/pull/29412)) by @Weiko
- Seat billing now uses max(committed seats, members minus free seats). Increases are charged immediately; decreases apply right away with a prorated credit. ([#29424](https://github.com/twentyhq/twenty/pull/29424)) by @etiennejouan
- Workspaces with a credit allowance arrangement receive a fixed monthly credit amount instead of the plan default, applied at the start of each billing period. ([#29426](https://github.com/twentyhq/twenty/pull/29426)) by @etiennejouan
- The workspace assistant's configured name and avatar now appear in inbox message headers, structured mentions, previews, and assistant controls. Self-hosters: deploy the updated server before rolling out the new client build. ([#29841](https://github.com/twentyhq/twenty/pull/29841)) by @bosiraphael
- Security and Privacy settings are reorganized: iframe origins and media access use add-from-above tables with favicons, the AI card links to the agents and model tiers it affects, and the Privacy tab opens with a cleaner compliance layout. ([#29950](https://github.com/twentyhq/twenty/pull/29950)) by @Bonapara
- AI chat and chat thread messages now share the same visual components for a consistent look. Per-message timestamps no longer appear in chat threads. ([#29966](https://github.com/twentyhq/twenty/pull/29966)) by @martmull

## 🐛 Bug fixes

- Claude thinking tokens were billed at about 1.7× the Anthropic rate; that is now corrected. Anthropic cache writes are also priced correctly from this version forward. ([#29976](https://github.com/twentyhq/twenty/pull/29976)) by @etiennejouan

title: sdk/v2.57.1
body:
<!-- generated-release-notes v1 -->

This release is mostly server and web-app work. Two changes touch SDK consumers directly.

AI component previews now run TypeScript semantic checks against your app's installed dependencies before esbuild. Type errors and source locations come back through the existing failure response, so the AI can correct mistakes before the preview runs.

The inbox message type gains two new fields: `AgentMessage.isBuiltInAssistant` and `senderApplicationId`. Deploy the server update before shipping the new client query.

## 🌟 Highlights

- AI component previews now type-check against your app's installed dependencies before esbuild; TypeScript errors and source locations are returned through the existing failure response. ([#29412](https://github.com/twentyhq/twenty/pull/29412))
- `AgentMessage` gains `isBuiltInAssistant` and `senderApplicationId` fields; the server must be deployed before the new client query ships. ([#29841](https://github.com/twentyhq/twenty/pull/29841))

## ✨ New features

- `AgentMessage` gains `isBuiltInAssistant` and `senderApplicationId` fields; deploy the server before updating the client SDK. ([#29841](https://github.com/twentyhq/twenty/pull/29841)) by @bosiraphael

body:
<!-- generated-release-notes v1 -->

AI chat can now build, preview, and publish frontend components in your workspace. Describe what you need, and the agent writes and renders it with sample data before asking for your approval. Five breaking changes ship with this release; API consumers and self-hosters should check that section before upgrading.

Records can now be made private. A private record is visible only to its creator and the people it is shared with directly. Roles do not reach it, including admin.

The LinkedIn app gained a Sync tab. It can import your conversation history and create or match People from contacts. Image, video, and audio attachments come along.

- Every webhook now requires a role. Pass a `roleId` when calling `createWebhook`, and provide the `ROLES` permission alongside `API_KEYS_AND_WEBHOOKS` to create or edit webhooks. ([#29273](https://github.com/twentyhq/twenty/pull/29273)) by @charlesBochet

Five breaking changes ship in this release. `createWebhook` requires a `roleId`. `objectMetadata.readability`, `writability`, and `sharingReach` are removed from GraphQL. `setRecordGeneralAccess` is replaced by `setRecordPrivate`. `IconsProvider` moves out of `twenty-ui/icon`, cutting ~2 MB from affected bundles. The workspace field `allowedIframeOrigins` is renamed.

`defineHealthCheck` gains `runOnUserPreferences: true` for member-scoped checks. App manifests accept `defineRelatedRecordPath`. The `SEND_CHAT_MESSAGE` workflow step now roundtrips through pull and apply.

`twenty local` is restored: `start`, `stop`, `status`, `logs`, `upgrade`, and `reset`. Validation failures now include the server's error code and friendly message. The CLI no longer rejects a manifest that references the workspace default role without a local definition.

- createWebhook now requires a roleId; updateWebhook accepts an optional roleId to change it; creating or editing a webhook now also requires the ROLES permission. ([#29273](https://github.com/twentyhq/twenty/pull/29273)) by @charlesBochet
- defineSettingsMenuItem now accepts an optional slug (lowercase kebab-case, max 64 chars) used as the URL hash for that settings tab; Connect and Reconnect now land on the app's first preferences tab. ([#29355](https://github.com/twentyhq/twenty/pull/29355)) by @martmull
- Replace setRecordGeneralAccess with setRecordPrivate(recordId, isPrivate) — a record is now either private (creator and direct shares only) or role-governed. ([#29383](https://github.com/twentyhq/twenty/pull/29383)) by @charlesBochet

- runMyApplicationHealthCheck(applicationId) is now available as a GraphQL mutation to trigger a member health check; it requires a user session and CONNECTED_ACCOUNTS. ([#29250](https://github.com/twentyhq/twenty/pull/29250)) by @ehconitin
- The SDK/CLI frontend component render wrapper now accepts compiled source and record props directly and returns a promise that resolves after the initial React commit. ([#29263](https://github.com/twentyhq/twenty/pull/29263)) by @Weiko
